Abstract
Atoms don't comprise nuclei and electron shells.
Nuclei don't comprise Z protons and (A ? Z) neutrons.
There are no perpetually spinning protons, neutrons and electrons.
Rutherford's scattering experiments and Moseley's X-ray experiments are not crucial for the nuclear atomic model. The same set of data can be explained by another atomic model.
The main characteristics of the Rutherford-Bohr-Chadwick nuclear atomic model are:
A nucleus, which is made up of Z protons and (A ? Z) neutrons, where A is mass number and Z is the atomic number of the periodic table
An electron cloud is located around the nucleus.
The Z extra nuclear electrons are placed in shells. The electron shells are arranged according to aufbau rules that determine spins and angular momenta of the electrons. Similar rules exist for the arrangement of nuclear shells. Both, scattering experiments with metal foils and X-ray experiments for nearly all elements were able to introduce the atomic number Z of target atoms as the variable of the corresponding metal foils or of the corresponding elements, respectively. This supposition is not justified because
Rutherford's scattering theory considers electrostatic scattering only and disregards therefore the magnetic scattering effect.
Most elements possess isotopes, which have obviously the same atomic number Z.
Rutherford left out of consideration isotope scattering experiments. According to Rutherford, the scattering of Sn-112 and Sn-124 (for example) is identical, but this is improbable, rather an isotope shift can be expected. Presumably, the isotope shift is due to magnetic scattering too. Consequently, it is not possible to infer that the distinctive property for scattering is atomic number Z

Title Physics Without Physical Constants
Author(s) Edward Kapuscik
Keywords physics, physical constants, electrodynamics, basic equations
Published 1994
Pages 387-391
Abstract
One of the most fundamental properties of both Newton's mechanics and Maxwell electrodynamics is the absence of any physical constants in their basic equations. All necessary constants appear only at the stage of applications of these theories to specific phenomena. This is one of the reasons of universality and generality of these theories since physical constants always reflect our ignorance in formulation of physical laws. Therefore primary equations of physics should not contain physical constants at all, including the fundamental ones.
Quantum mechanics and general relativity seem to be counterexamples of the above requirement since Schroedinger equation contains both the fundamental Planck constant and the mass of the particle and Einstein equation contains the gravitational constant. It is however possible to suspect that both these great theories may be in some sense secondary and their basic equations may be derived from more fundamental formulations in which all physical constants do not appear.

Abstract
This paper develops a blueprint for the historical development of physics in general, highlighting present-day contributions from NPA participants in particular. The metaphor for physics as a building project involves a number of unwieldy building blocks in not-completely-stable relation to each other. Stresses and strains are pointed out, and redesign/rebuilding efforts are recommended.
Overview
This is a conference presentation by Cynthia Kolb Whitney , then editor of Galilean Electrodynamics and of the Proceedings of the NPA , delivered in slide form. Its device is a single sustained metaphor: physics is a building whose blocks were laid in the order historical accident supplied them rather than in the order a designer would have chosen, so that some blocks overhang their supports and some towers are visibly unstable. The exercise is to draw the elevation, mark the stresses, and say which parts need rebuilding.
The essay is unusual among dissident critiques in that it is structural rather than doctrinal. Whitney does not argue that any one theory is false; she argues that the load path is wrong — that theories are resting on foundations they do not actually match, and that the overhang is where the anomalies live. The second half turns from diagnosis to her own proposed repair, a model of light propagation she calls Two-Step Light, and closes with a short companion piece, "Mainstreaming — A Personal Progress Report," on how she got such work into mainstream journals.

Physics of the Dark Matter: The Proton Magnet is a 2017 book by the American engineer Michael Twichell , self-published through BookPatch LLC. It is the sequel to The Twichell Manuscript - Volume I: Aether Gravity and, at 457 pages, is substantially the longer of the two.
Where the first volume proposed a mechanism for gravity, this one extends the same full-space model — a universe filled with a material aether rather than empty space — to magnetism, force and inertia . Its organising device is a "Proton Magnet" model , which Twichell presents as simplifying chemistry and as accounting for quantum mechanics in ordinary language rather than in the formalism he regards as needlessly obscure.
The book is framed explicitly against academic physics: it presents itself as setting out knowledge it treats as plain but that conventional theory has left unexplained, and it argues that the empty-space model inherited from relativity is the source of the difficulty.
Reception
Like its predecessor the book was self-published and not peer reviewed, and it has no presence in the physics literature. The term "dark matter" is used here in the author's own sense, within his aether model, and not as the term is used in observational cosmology. This wiki records the argument as its author states it.

It is the best-known mainstream trade book about outsider and dissident physics, and is built around the work of James Carter — the trailer-park owner, former abalone diver and self-taught theorist known in the book as Jim Carter. She followed one of them, James Carter , for about a decade, and his story supplies the book's spine.
Carter rejects the whole line of orthodox development from Newton through Einstein and replaces it with a thoroughly mechanical picture of nature. Abstract
The number of paradoxes in theoretical physics is large. This means that we have reason to suspect that experiments have been interpreted in error long time ago. The behavior of light and ether has been misunderstood. This has caused wrong interpretations of stellar aberration, Michelson and Morley's tests and of Einstein's so called light clock. If we instead regard Sagnac effect, global positioning system (GPS), Pioneer anomaly, gravitational anomalies during solar eclipses and the behavior of atomic clocks, than we get a very different view of light and ether. Overview
John-Erik Persson argues that a long chain of paradoxes in modern physics traces to a misreading of a small number of nineteenth-century experiments, and that with those readings corrected the ether returns and relativity becomes unnecessary.
His central technical claim is that a transverse ether wind — one blowing within the plane of a wave front — is undetectable in any apparatus that senses phase rather than amplitude. Telescopes and interferometers detect by phase, so only the longitudinal component of the wind, parallel to the propagation direction, can influence them. From this he concludes that the Michelson–Morley experiment could never have detected the effect it was designed for, that Einstein's light-clock argument repeats the same error, and that stellar aberration tells us nothing about the ether at all — only about the state of motion of the telescope.

Pierre-Marie Luc Robitaille is a Canadian-American scientist, Professor of Radiology at The Ohio State University from 1989 to 2019, who designed and built the world's first Ultra High Field human MRI scanner — and who then turned the physics he had learned from that machine against some of the central claims of modern astrophysics.
He argues that Kirchhoff's law of thermal emission is invalid in its universal form; that the Sun is therefore not a gaseous plasma but condensed matter — liquid metallic hydrogen ; and that the cosmic microwave background attributed to the Big Bang is in fact the thermal signature of the Earth's own oceans .
Robitaille is unusual among the researchers documented here in that his dissent grew directly out of a major mainstream achievement. He did not approach thermal physics as an outsider but as the builder of an instrument whose behaviour, in his account, could not be reconciled with the textbook law.

Linear and rotary motions of a macro body are entirely separate. Each of them is produced by separate set of work-done on a macro body. However, each matter particle of a linearly moving, rotating macro body has its own path of resultant motion. Its motion and path appear to be resultant of linear and rotary motions of the macro body. A preferred frame — also called a privileged frame or absolute frame — is a frame of reference singled out from all others, in which the laws of physics take their simplest form and against which motion can be called absolute rather than merely relative.
Whether such a frame exists is one of the oldest and sharpest divisions in physics, and it is the question on which a large part of the literature catalogued on this wiki turns.
The mainstream view
Modern physics holds that there is no preferred frame .
The position rests on the principle of relativity : the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames, so no experiment performed inside a uniformly moving laboratory can reveal its motion. Special relativity builds this in as a postulate, together with the invariance of the speed of light, and derives the Lorentz transformation from the two. General relativity extends the equivalence to accelerated frames.
The historical turning point is taken to be the Michelson–Morley experiment of 1887, whose failure to detect the Earth's motion through a stationary aether is read as evidence that no such medium — and so no frame attached to it — exists. Lorentz's aether theory preserved a preferred frame but made it undetectable in principle, and was set aside as carrying an unobservable entity to no predictive advantage. On the standard account the two theories agree on every observation, and special relativity is preferred for its economy.
Mainstream physics does allow that some frames are distinguished without being dynamically preferred. Inertial frames are collectively privileged over rotating and accelerating ones, since only the latter require causes outside the system — Newton's rotating bucket and Einstein's spinning spheres make the point. And the cosmic microwave background defines a frame in which its radiation is isotropic, relative to which the Earth's motion is measured at about 370 km/s. This is treated as a contingent fact about the distribution of matter

Prime Matter Particles is the particle theory proposed by the American comic-book artist and independent theorist Neal Adams (1941–2022) to supply the missing mechanism for his Growing Earth — the proposition that the Earth and the other bodies of the solar system are steadily increasing in size and mass because new matter is continuously created within them.
Adams held that there is only one kind of particle in the universe, which he called the prime matter particle . The particle is a bound electron–positron unit; the electron and the positron are not two species but two halves of the one thing, separated only when a prime matter particle is broken. An unbroken ocean of these particles, he argued, fills space from edge to edge, and the process conventionally called pair production is not the creation of a pair from energy but the splitting of a prime matter particle that was already there. Where a natural magnetic field keeps the halves apart instead of letting them recombine, the result is new matter — and in the core of a planet that new matter accumulates, so the planet grows.
The theory is Adams' answer to the standing objection against expansion tectonics: that the reconstructions may look convincing but no known process can add the required mass. It is the least accepted part of his work, and the part from which even most expansion researchers on this wiki keep their distance while accepting the geological case.

"Proof the Universe is Infinite—A Non Sequitur" is an article by Glenn Borchardt published on 3 November 2025 on The Scientific Worldview .
Asked what irrefutable proof exists that the universe is infinite, Borchardt concedes there is none and argues the demand is misconceived. Infinity and finity are opposed fundamental assumptions, neither provable nor falsifiable, though if one is true the other is false. Complete proof is unobtainable precisely because the universe is infinite: no measurement can ever be repeated exactly, and we are always dealing with less than the whole.

The proton is the positively charged particle found in every atomic nucleus, and the sole nucleus of ordinary hydrogen. It was identified by Ernest Rutherford between 1917 and 1920 as the hydrogen nucleus knocked out of nitrogen by alpha bombardment, and given its present name in 1920. Its charge is + e , equal and opposite to that of the electron ; its mass is about 1836 times the electron's, or 938.3 MeV/ c 2 ; its spin is ½. The number of protons in a nucleus fixes the chemical element, so the proton is the quantity that the periodic table is ordered by.
In the Standard Model the proton is not elementary. It is a baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark bound by gluons, and only a small fraction of its mass comes from the quark masses themselves — the great majority is attributed to the binding energy of the colour field. The proton is the only baryon believed to be stable: grand unified theories predict that it should eventually decay, but no decay has ever been observed, and experiments such as Super-Kamiokande place the lifetime above roughly 10 34 years.
Two features of the standard picture are unsettled within mainstream physics itself, and both are worth stating plainly because they are often raised in the literature below. The first is the proton spin problem : deep inelastic scattering measurements from the late 1980s onward found that the spins of the three quarks account for only about a third of the proton's total spin, the remainder being assigned to gluon spin and orbital motion in ways still under investigation. The second is the proton radius puzzle : the charge radius measured from ordinary hydrogen and from electron scattering had settled near 0.88 femtometres when a 2010 measurement using muonic hydrogen returned about 0.84 fm, a discrepancy far outside the quoted errors. Abstract
Millisecond pulsar timing algorithms place all measurements into a solar-centered reference frame, which is assumed to be inertial with respect to the Earth, after correcting the Earth's motion to that of a perfectly circular orit in a constant gravitational field. However, this analysis is valid only if the pulsar exhibits no proper motion with respect to solar barycenter. Since this is likely never to be the case, a relativistic correction must be made to account for the Earth's constantly changing velocity with respect to the reference frame of the pulsar source. This correction takes the form of a periodic timing residual, on the order or microseconds, which should be detectable through the use of pulsar timing arrays, low period pulsars with large proper motions. The absence of such a residual may constitute a failure of special relativity.

Push versus pull is the question of whether anything in nature ever pulls . Every textbook force can attract: gravitation attracts always, electrostatic and magnetic forces attract in half of their cases, and the nuclear forces bind. A tradition that runs through this collection from Newton to the present holds that not one of these is really a pull — that a body cannot reach across a gap and draw another towards it, and that wherever attraction is observed something is arriving from outside and pushing .
The claim is not that the equations are wrong. Almost everyone making it keeps Coulomb's law and the inverse square. The claim is about what the equations describe: whether the minus sign in front of an attractive potential names a real tug, or bookkeeping for an imbalance in a pressure that is doing all the work.
The standard account
Modern physics recognises four interactions and has no objection in principle to any of them attracting. A force is derived from a potential, and the direction in which a body moves is decided by the sign of the potential's gradient; nothing in the formalism prefers repulsion. In quantum field theory the interaction is carried by exchange, and attraction between unlike charges is as ordinary a result as repulsion between like ones. In general relativity gravity is not a force at all: bodies follow geodesics of a geometry shaped by mass-energy, so the question of what pulls does not arise.
The mainstream position on the old objection — that attraction requires action at a distance — is that field theory answered it in the nineteenth century. The field is local, it carries energy and momentum of its own, and each body responds to the field where it is. Nothing crosses empty space instantaneously, and nothing reaches.
What the standard account does not supply is a mechanism in the mechanical sense: an account of how the field draws the body, in terms of something happening in the space between. That the field is the mediator is an answer

Quasars (quasi-stellar objects, or QSOs) are compact, extremely luminous objects with very large redshifts . They are the single most contested class of object in modern cosmology, and the principal battleground between standard cosmology and the critical tradition documented on this wiki.
Mainstream astronomy reads a quasar's large redshift as purely cosmological, and therefore places quasars at the greatest distances in the observable universe — making them the most luminous objects known. A substantial body of observational work, led above all by the astronomer Halton C Arp , contends that this interpretation is mistaken: that quasars are far nearer than assumed , that much of their redshift is intrinsic rather than cosmological, and that they are ejected from the nuclei of active nearby galaxies . If so, the redshift–distance relation fails precisely where cosmology most depends on it, and the Big Bang distance scale must be rebuilt.
The standard picture
On the conventional account a quasar is the nucleus of a young, distant galaxy powered by matter accreting onto a supermassive black hole. Its redshift is taken to arise wholly from cosmic expansion, placing typical quasars billions of light-years away, and requiring luminosities hundreds of times that of an entire galaxy. This is the interpretation found in textbooks and assumed by most survey work.

Abstract
The "Big Bang" model has ascended to a powerful position in modern cosmology over the past few decades. This position has become so strong that investigation of alternate ideas has almost ceased. Observational counter-evidence certainly exists (for reviews see e.g. Arp 1987; Sulentic 1987; Tifft 1987). The general belief is that this counter-evidence consists of misinterpreted data and false clues. One could easily get the impression that all of the observations fit easily into the accepted model. In fact, at least three new concepts have assumed great importance in preserving the Big Bang against observational and theoretical challenges. In temporal order of acclamation they are: 1) black holes; 2) merger phenomena and 3) dark matter. Gravitational accretiion onto supermassive black holes was required as soon as it became generally accepted that the quasar redshifts were cosmological (i.e. proportional to their distance). It provides a mechanism for producing the enormous energies implied by the assumption that quasars are at their redshift distances. Mergers came upon the scene in order to account for nearby peculiar galaxies and for the increasing luminosity and size of many objects at higher redshift. Dark matter helps to bind the groups and clusters of galaxies as well as to explain the flat rotation curves in spirals. In reality, it can help to fit almost any observation into the conventional picture. What is the observational evidence for the above three phenomena?

Quirino Majorana (1871-1957) was an outstanding Italian experimental physicist who investigated a wide range of phenomena during his long career as professor of physics at the Universities of Rome, Turin (1916-1921), and Bologna (1921-1934), Italy. He is remembered above all for a long series of extremely sensitive experiments on gravitational absorption - the claim that a body's weight is measurably reduced when heavy matter is interposed between it and the Earth - and for a parallel programme of optical experiments intended to test Albert Einstein's postulate of the constancy of the speed of light. Openly critical of relativity, Majorana pursued both questions as an experimentalist rather than a theorist, and his gravitational results remain among the most-cited unreplicated experiments in the literature of alternative gravity.

From 1904 to 1914 he directed the Central Institute of Telephones and Telegraphs in Rome, an appointment that shaped his lifelong interest in applied electricity, radiotelephony and early television.

Abstract
The "Electric Universe" Theory (EUT) owes part of its inspiration to the work of Immanuel Velikovsky ( Worlds in Collision [1950]), at least for introducing the concept of catastrophism of an electrical nature potentially inducing what EUT proponents see as plasma-arced "scarring" on some planets and other objects within our solar system, such as Mars. Though discredited by mainstream physicists and astronomers since the publication of his ideas in 1950, Velikovsky nonetheless ushered in an era where catastrophic events, rather than just immeasurable eons of uniformitarianism, became acknowledged as a potential contributor to the current state of our solar system (and maybe beyond). Based on my admittedly quite crude calculations in this paper, it still appears too far-fetched to believe the planet Venus arose out of Jupiter and careened through the inner solar system anytime within human history (if ever at all). However, this does not invalidate the EUT contention that planetary scarring due to electrical plasma-arcing may be responsible for the bizarre surface features seen on Mars and perhaps other celestial objects. But just what particular planetoids or comets might have been responsible for this remains unknown.
Overview
Re-Examining Velikovsky is a three-page paper by Raymond H Gallucci , dated 2013 and later presented at the CNPS 2015 conference. It asks whether Immanuel Velikovsky's claim in Worlds in Collision (1950) — that Venus was ejected from Jupiter and passed close to Mars and Earth within human memory — survives a simple physical check, while keeping open the Electric Universe proposal that plasma arcing scarred planetary surfaces.

This paper provides a physical systems model for the transmission of all forces that appear to act through a distance in an absolute vacuum, and for redefining the essence of nuclear particulate matter. The basic elements of this model are the existence of isotropic radiant frequencies in free space and in matter, and matter existing as interference patterns or deformations in the linear flows. Matter's shadowing interactions with these non particulate radiant spectra cause forces of attraction and repulsion. A free body in open space is symmetrically illuminated with this radiant flow, and as it shields or shadows some of the radiation passing through it, the resultant forces are also symmetrically balanced. Ralph E. Juergens (6 May 1924 – 2 November 1979) was an American civil engineer and technical editor, remembered for two things: his part in documenting the scientific establishment's treatment of Immanuel Velikovsky , and his proposal that the Sun is powered electrically rather than by nuclear fusion.
The second is the more consequential. In 1972 he argued that the Sun is not a self-contained thermonuclear furnace but the focus of a cosmic electric discharge, drawing its radiant energy from the galaxy around it. Astrophysics does not accept the idea, but it became the founding statement of the electric Sun model and, through that, of the electric universe literature; Wallace Thornhill has written that the electric universe model "follows the brilliant work of Ralph Juergens".
Velikovsky himself never accepted it. The thermonuclear account of the Sun seemed sound to him, and he declined to follow the man who had done more than almost anyone to defend him.
Biography
Education
B.S. — Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland. He trained as a civil engineer
Career
Juergens worked as an editor in the publications division of McGraw-Hill. By de Grazia 's account he gave up that work in 1960 and moved from the Midwest to Hightstown, New Jersey, near Princeton, in order to take up Velikovsky's work; he later lived in Arizona.
He was Associate Editor of Pensée and a Senior Editor of Kronos , the two journals in which most of his writing appeared.
The Velikovsky affair
Velikovsky suggested to the writer Alfred de Grazia that Juergens serve as science editor for a book they were planning on Velikovsky's treatment by scientists, with the historian of science Livio Stecchini writing the historical part.

Scientific career
Fields Mathematical physics
Ralph G. Beil (born 1938) is an American mathematical physicist. Over some two decades he developed a programme that uses Finsler geometry to construct a unified field theory, deriving electromagnetism and other interactions from the geometry of the tangent bundle. The Beil metric , a Finsler metric he introduced for this purpose, is named after him and has been taken up by later workers in the field.
Scientific work
Beil's work belongs to the tradition, going back to Weyl, Kaluza and Klein, of seeking to unify the forces of physics within an enlarged geometry. His distinctive move was to base that geometry not on ordinary Riemannian spacetime but on Finsler geometry — a generalization in which the metric can depend on direction as well as position — and to build it on the tangent bundle of spacetime.
In a sequence of papers beginning in the late 1980s he argued that a physical motivation for Finsler structure can be developed through gauge transformations on the tangent space, producing a correspondence in which geometric objects — metrics, connections and curvatures — play the roles of the physical gauge potentials, fields and energy-momentum. From this he recovered electrodynamics "from a metric," treated the classical charged particle as an extended geometric object, and extended the scheme toward the electroweak interaction with his work on "electroweak symmetry on the tangent bundle." The Beil metric introduced in this programme has since been studied by other geometers as a basis for unified field theories. Beil presented the approach at the 1995 Joint Summer Research Conference on Finsler Geometry, published in the American Mathematical Society volume Finsler Geometry (1996).

Ralph Sansbury is an American physicist and independent researcher based in Larchmont, New York, whose work centres on a single hypothesis: that electric dipoles induced inside atomic nuclei and inside electrons underlie phenomena conventionally assigned to magnetism, gravitation and the finite speed of light.
After graduating from the University of Chicago he taught at the University of Illinois and at the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn, and worked as a researcher at MIT's magnet laboratory. He has published in the Review of Scientific Instruments , the Journal of Classical Physics and the Optics Testing Digest , and holds patents relating to the applied side of his work, in nuclear fusion and ion separation.
Education
University of Chicago
Research
Nuclear electric dipoles
Sansbury's central proposal is that an atomic nucleus is not an inert charge but contains a small orbital component — he estimates its mass at around 10 −55 kg — which can be displaced by an applied electric force to leave the nucleus polarised. Because ordinary matter's outer electrons screen static fields, he argues that polarisation survives only where the applied force is changing, which he takes to be the general case in rotating and orbiting bodies.
His experimental contribution is a 1985 paper in the Review of Scientific Instruments reporting a force between a charged metal foil and a current-carrying conductor — an effect not predicted by standard electrodynamics, since a neutral current-carrying wire should exert no net electrostatic force. Claims of this general kind have a small literature; the best known, by Edwards and collaborators in 1976, was not confirmed by later searches.

Careaga's cosmological writing follows the plasma tradition of Hannes Alfvén , Winston H Bostick and Anthony L Peratt : that the universe is overwhelmingly plasma, that electric currents and magnetic fields shape its structure, and that cosmology should be extrapolated from laboratory plasma behaviour rather than from gravity alone. On that basis he rejects the Big Bang , dark matter and dark energy, and treats the objects called black holes as plasmoid phenomena of a kind produced in the laboratory since the 1950s.
What distinguishes EPEMC from plasma cosmology proper is its deliberate breadth. Gallucci (born December 15, 1953) is an American nuclear engineer and a dissident-science author who has written extensively for the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society (CNPS/JCNPS), critiquing mainstream relativity and cosmology. He holds a PhD in nuclear engineering and is a licensed Professional Engineer (PE). Much of his independent work applies elementary mathematical analysis to test whether the theories advanced by other dissident scientists are at least plausible – an unusual role within the dissident community, where most authors advance a theory of their own rather than auditing those of their colleagues.
Biography
Gallucci was born in Albany, New York, and resides in Frederick, Maryland. His formal training required extensive study of physics, particularly atomic and nuclear physics, and during his university years he developed an additional interest in relativity, quantum physics, and astronomy.
He is a licensed Professional Engineer and completed a roughly 40-year career in nuclear power, in both the commercial and governmental sectors, including work at the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission in the area of probabilistic safety assessment. Year 1929 onward
Redshift is the observed shift of spectral lines from distant astronomical objects toward longer (redder) wavelengths, conventionally denoted z . It is the single most consequential measurement in modern cosmology: the entire extragalactic distance scale, the expansion of the universe, and the Big Bang itself all rest on one particular interpretation of what redshift means.
That interpretation — that redshift is essentially a velocity effect, so that a larger redshift means a greater distance and a faster recession — is precisely what the critical tradition documented on this wiki disputes. The observation itself is not in question; the inference from it is. A substantial body of work catalogued here argues that redshift can be produced by several physical processes that have nothing to do with recession, that some redshift is intrinsic to the object, and that in consequence redshift is not a reliable measure of distance — which would remove the observational foundation of the expanding-universe model.
The observation
When light from a distant source is dispersed into a spectrum, the characteristic absorption and emission lines of known elements appear at longer wavelengths than they do in the laboratory. The fractional shift, z = Δλ⁄λ, is straightforward to measure and is not itself controversial. Everything that follows depends on what is held to cause it.

The resulting expressions contain both gravitational and velocity components, but — in contrast to the conventional model — the gravitational term dominates. Redshifts are associated with very dense objects at almost any speed relative to Σ, and with normal stars at low speeds in Σ; on the other hand, blueshifts correspond to low density objects moving at high speeds in Σ. These results contrast with the conventional model where red/blueshifts are associated with recession/approximation from/to us. The present model predicts that photons may escape from extremely high-density objects, thus eliminating the concept of black holes. There is no connection assumed between redshift and distance, so that high-redshift objects may be associated with objects having smaller redshifts. Also, our theoretical equation for frequency shifts is completely consistent with the phenomenological equation describing the observed periodicity in the redshift of quasars, suggesting that such objects may be formed by an integer number of neutron stars, moving at speeds around 0.5c relative to Σ.

Keywords redshift periodicity, quantization, Karlsson peaks, galactocentric, intrinsic redshift, Big Bang
Year 1976 onward
Redshift quantization , also called redshift periodicity , is the claim that the redshifts of galaxies and quasars are not distributed smoothly but cluster around preferred, regularly spaced values . If the claim holds, it is difficult to reconcile with redshift as a simple measure of recession velocity, since a genuine distribution of velocities and distances should be continuous. It is therefore among the strongest observational arguments for an intrinsic , non-velocity component in redshift, and against the Big Bang interpretation of the redshift–distance relation.
The observational claim
The effect was first reported by the astronomer William G Tifft of the University of Arizona in the 1970s, who found that galaxy redshifts appeared to fall into steps rather than a continuum. Subsequent work identified periodicities of roughly 72 km/s and various submultiples.
The most careful confirmations came from Bruce Guthrie and William Napier, who in 1990 reported a periodicity of similar magnitude in a sample restricted to bright spiral galaxies. Their final analysis concluded that extragalactic redshifts are quantized in the galactocentric frame of reference — that is, after correcting for the Sun's motion within our own galaxy — with periodicities of about 37.5 km/s among field galaxies and loose groups, and about 71.1 km/s in dense cluster environments. They argued the result could not be attributed to statistical artefacts, selection procedures, or flawed reduction techniques.
For quasars, K. G. Karlsson reported in 1971 a periodicity in log(1 + z ), producing preferred values near z ≈ 0.061, 0.30, 0.60, 0.96, 1.41 and 1.96 — the Karlsson peaks . Halton C Arp regarded these as dir

Title Reference-Frame Independent Dynamics, Or How to Get Off Einstein's Train
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) Greg Volk
Keywords Hertzian Electromagnetism, convective derivative, reference frame, Mach's Principle, universal instant, Maxwell's equations
Published 2009
No. of pages 12
Abstract
Einstein spent his life trying to develop a system of dynamics independent of reference frame. But this lofty goal demands a hard look at the very meaning of reference frame, a starting point for this paper. Einstein's fruitless attempts were based on his own observer-based theory of relativity, in turn based on Lorentzian covariant paradigms. Covariant mathematics admits transformations between coordinate systems and reference frames, but does not suggest a path towards invariance. However, the del operator provides a means of expressing spatial derivatives independent of coordinate system. Likewise, if time is independent of space, as this paper suggests, the total time derivative operator, d/dt, is also independent of reference frame. Therefore, physical equations that can be expressed with the del operator and the total time derivative, as opposed to reference-frame dependent partial derivatives, are naturally independent of reference frame. In particular, Maxwell's equations can be correct only if expressible by the del and d/dt operators, as proposed by Hertz and more recently advocated by Phipps. From fluid dynamics, developed by Bernoulli, Euler, Langrange, and many others, over a hundred years before Maxwell, we have the convective or Lagrangian time derivative d/dt = d/dt + v • del. Both sides of this equality are independent of observer, but the two right-hand terms differ in weight depending on how an observer moves with respect to the quantity being differentiated. One observer might see a buildup of material, while another sees an altered flow; one observer might see a changing field, another an acceleration. But the total change, the sum, remains invariant.

Reginald Irvan Gray , O.B.E. (18 March 1917 – 28 November 1996), was an English-born research physicist and former Royal Air Force officer who, after emigrating to the United States, worked as an experimental and theoretical physicist for the United States Navy . He is best remembered among independent-science circles for his lifelong study of classical electromagnetism in the tradition of James Clerk Maxwell , for a series of experiments probing fundamental questions such as the finite mass of the photon and the possible presence of neutrinos in the vacuum, and for his book Unified Physics (1988).
Biography
Gray served during the Second World War as a Group Captain in the Royal Air Force and was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire ( O.B.E. ). He was counted among "the few," the RAF airmen of the wartime generation, and by contemporaries was described as an exceptionally modest man who seldom spoke of his wartime service.
After the war Gray emigrated to the United States, where he was employed as a physicist at a U.S. Navy laboratory. He became known within the community of independent physicists from the late 1960s onward, carrying out carefully crafted experiments—initially on his own initiative and later with some support from his laboratory. He settled in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, and continued both experimental and theoretical work through his years of retirement until his death in 1996.
Scientific contributions
Gray's work centred on classical electromagnetic theory and its experimental application. He was noted for a detailed command of nineteenth-century physics, including Maxwell 's Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism and the work of J. J. Thomson , which he combined with an interest in contemporary developments in physics.

Relational Mechanics is a 1999 book by the physicist André K. T. Assis , published by Apeiron (Montreal). It is the English-language statement of his relational-mechanics programme (later expanded in the Portuguese Mecânica Relacional ).
Overview
Relational mechanics is presented as a new mechanics intended to replace Einstein's theories of relativity. It implements Mach's principle quantitatively, using a Weber-type relational law for gravitation together with a principle of dynamical equilibrium, and expresses all dynamics through relational quantities (distances and relative velocities/accelerations between bodies). Assis shows how the framework accounts for Newton's bucket experiment as a gravitational interaction between the water and the distant matter of the universe in relative rotation, and derives inertia from that same cosmic interaction. The book is addressed to physicists, engineers, mathematicians, and historians and philosophers of science.
About the author
André Koch Torres Assis is a Brazilian physicist at the University of Campinas (Unicamp) known for his work on Weber's electrodynamics, Mach's principle, and the history and foundations of physics.

Put one particle in an otherwise empty universe and there is nothing for spacetime to do but bow toward it everywhere. Abstract
The satellites of the global positioning system (GPS) travel around the earth in 12-hour periods in near-circular orbits. All of the satellites contain extremely precise atomic clocks whose rates depend both upon satellite velocity and altitude. An observer bound to the earth, in an airplane or in a satellite may determine his precise location by obtaining signals from several satellites simultaneously. Overview
This is the first of two papers in which Ronald R. Hatch takes the three effects Ashby treats — velocity effects on clock rate, gravitational-potential effects on clock rate, and the Sagnac Effect — and argues that Ashby's explanation of each is "patently incorrect", even where the numerical result is right.
His central claim is one of frame dependence. GPS does not adjust satellite and receiver clocks according to their relative velocity, as the special theory would require; it adjusts them according to their velocity with respect to a chosen frame, the earth-centred non-rotating frame. Marmet notes correctly that for a radially infalling particle the two are related by dt/dτ = (1 − 2M/r) −1 , and observes that the falling observer crosses in moments while the distant observer never sees the crossing at all.
He then makes the argument quantitative with a worked figure. Taking a star that forms "in 10 million years in proper time", he synchronises the two clocks at large r and follows the infall. Abstract
Currently, the theory of Relativity is being regarded as one of the main pillars of Modern Physics, essentially due to its perceived role in high energy physics, particle accelerators, relativistic quantum mechanics, and cosmology. Since the founding assumptions or postulates of Relativity and some of the resulting consequences confound the logic and common sense, a growing number of scientists are now questioning the validity of Relativity. The advent of Relativity has also ruled out the existence of the 19th century notion of ether medium or physical space as the container of physical reality. Thereby, the Newtonian notions of absolute motion, absolute time, and absolute reference frame have been replaced with the Einsteinian notions of relative motion, relative time, and inertial reference frames in relative motion. This relativity dominated viewpoint has effectively abandoned any critical study or advanced research in the detailed properties and processes of physical space for advancement of Fundamental Physics. In this paper both special theory of relativity and general relativity have been critically examined for their current relevance and future potential. We find that even though Relativity appears to be a major stumbling block in the progress of Modern Physics, the issue needs to be finally settled by a viable experiment [Phys. Essays 23, 442 (2010)] that can detect absolute motion and establish a universal reference frame.

Abstract
A simple scheme for ordering the facts of physics is presented, and some terms associated with basic research are introduced. Some aspects of this research are discussed and an outline of a simple model as an example of a working hypothesis for explaining the known facts is proposed. <o:p></o:p>
Overview
This ten-page essay is Jozef Kajfosz 's statement of method rather than of physics. Written in Polish in 1980, never submitted to a journal, posted on a web site and translated into English in 2013, it proposes a simple geometrical scheme — a triangle of facts — for ordering everything physics knows, uses that scheme to define what a "basic discovery" would be, states three rules such a discovery would have to satisfy, and then offers a deliberately unfinished model of the unknown as an illustration of what obeying those rules might look like.
Kajfosz's complaint is not that any particular theory is wrong. It is that the questions at the foundations of physics have no institutional home. The philosophy of science handles them so formally that it "does not reach the average physicist"; physicists themselves raise them "rarely and reluctantly," at seminars "regarded to be not fully serious," in popular works, or at jubilees — because "an unwritten social code says that it is necessary to be a physicist of a very high rank in order to be allowed to take up such a subject. But it seems that the opposite should be right."
The second and more distinctive theme is visuality . Kajfosz argues that physics since Maxwell has progressively abandoned demonstrative models in favour of pure description, and that this is a real loss of understanding rather than a maturation. Abstract
Theoretical aspects of VMD and related approaches to real photon-hadron interaction are discussed. The work relies on special relativity, properties of linearly polarized photons, angular momentum conservation and relevant experiments. It is explained why VMD and similar approaches should not be regarded as part of a theory but, at most, as phenomenological models. A further experiment pertaining to this issue is suggested.
Overview
E. Comay's 2003 Apeiron paper is a critique of Vector Meson Dominance (VMD) and the family of related ideas he groups together as "Photon's Hadronic Structure Approaches" (PHSA). The experimental facts these approaches were built to explain are not in dispute and Comay states them plainly: the cross section for hard photons scattered from a proton target is practically the same as from a neutron target, and the number of hadrons emitted from a photon–proton interaction region exceeds the leptonic number by four orders of magnitude. Something about the photon's behaviour at high energy is strongly hadron-like and largely independent of the target's electric charge.
What Comay attacks is the theoretical construction erected on top of those facts — the claim that a physical photon is a superposition of a pure electromagnetic component and a hadronic component,
| γ > = c 0 | γ 0 > + c h | h >,
with the fluctuation between the two treated as an inherent property of the photon, independent of its distance from any hadronic target, and the relative time spent in each state given by the squared moduli of the coefficients. In most versions | h > is a neutral vector meson carrying the photon's spin, parity and charge-conjugation quantum numbers; in Gribov's variant it may belong to a larger set of hadronic states.

"Replacing Coulombs with Meters" is an article by Jeff Yee published on 23 March 2019 on Beyond Mainstream .
Yee argues that naming units after Coulomb, Newton, Ampere and Tesla, while a fitting honour, has helped keep the electrical and mechanical domains of physics apart: a student meeting a named unit is less likely to ask what it actually measures. Most such units reduce to simpler SI terms — the ampere to coulombs per second — and he contends that one unit in particular, once simplified, bridges the gap between the two domains.

Replacing Special Relativity By John Hodge was a live session on 6 April 2024 in the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society live session series.
Re-interpreting the experiments that formed the base of Special Relativity.
Summary
John Hodge supplied a recorded video applying the Scalar Theory of Everything to the observations on which special relativity was built, and intended to answer questions afterwards. His connection failed repeatedly before, during and after the recording; he was never able to speak for more than a few seconds, sent no answers to the chat, and the session was ended early. Roger J Anderton hosted, with Franklin Hu filling in.
The video
Hodge's method is to go back to the nineteenth-century experiments — Fizeau's on the index of refraction of moving water, stellar aberration, and Michelson–Morley — and to read the data rather than the conclusions drawn from them.
Fizeau. Light speed increases with the flow and decreases against it. Hodge calls this carry-along rather than drag: the speed of light depends on the local plenum density, greater density giving greater tension and a higher speed, so a photon moving with the fluid spends more of its time on the relative peak and one moving against it in the relative valley.
Michelson–Morley. Hodge put up the graph from the original paper and made an observation about its shape. The differences are not in the east–west direction, where the result is very nearly null, but in the directions corresponding to the Sun–Moon combination — which, he suggested tentatively, makes the residual a tidal effect rather than a motion-through-the-ether effect, and another instance of carry-along from nearby bodies: the table, the room, the Sun and the Moon. Author(s) Glen W Deen

Published 2007
Journal Proceedings of the NPA
Volume 5
Number 1
Pages 43-45
Abstract
Anderson et al. say: ?We have reported an anomalous, constant acceleration of Pioneer 10 and 11, a = (8.74 "1.33)E-8 cm/s 2 , directed towards the Sun, at distances ~20 - 70 AU." This anomaly can be reproduced by a multi-layer, onion-like, spherical cosmic lens centered on the Sun with an inner radius of 20 AU. If the effect stops at around 70 AU then the lens has eight layers, and the outer radius of the lens is 68.58 AU, and the effective refraction index through the eight layers is 1.000587235. If the effect extends beyond 70 AU, then there are more than eight layers. The innermost layer has a thickness of 3.33 AU and a refraction index of 1.000067963, and the eighth layer has a thickness of 9.79 AU and a refraction index of 1.000155628. The ratios between the volumes of adjacent lens layers is a constant, and that constant is within 0.2% of 4 1/3 . In order to make the volume ratios exactly equal to 4 1/3 , the anomaly error bars need to change from ?1.3300 to ?1.3357. The anomalous acceleration towards the Sun is just the calculated "observed" acceleration minus the Newtonian acceleration. The Newtonian acceleration is simply a = GM/R 2 , where GM is the heliocentric gravitation constant, and R is the radial distance from the Sun to the spacecraft. The calculated "observed" acceleration is just the Newtonian acceleration times the effective index of refraction at the spacecraft's location. The effective index of refraction is the product of the individual layer refraction indexes that are interior to the spacecraft's location.

Title Resolving Spacecraft Earth-Flyby Anomalies with Measured Light Speed Anisotropy
Author(s) Reginald T Cahill
Keywords light speed , spacecraft
Published 2008
Journal Progress In Physics
Volume 3
Number July, 2008
Pages 9-15
Abstract
Doppler shift observations of spacecraft, such as Galileo, NEAR, Cassini, Rosetta and MESSENGER in earth flybys, have all revealed unexplained speed "anomalies" - that the Doppler-shift determined speeds are inconsistent with expected speeds. Here it is shown that these speed anomalies are not real and are actually the result of using an incorrect relationship between the observed Doppler shift and the speed of the spacecraft - a relationship based on the assumption that the speed of light is isotropic in all frames, viz invariant. Taking account of the repeatedly measured light-speed anisotropy the anomalies are resolved ab initio. The Pioneer 10/11 anomalies are discussed, but not resolved. The spacecraft observations demonstrate again that the speed of light is not invariant, and is isotropic only with respect to a dynamical 3-space. The existing Doppler shift data also o ers a resource to characterise a new form of gravitational waves, the dynamical 3-space turbulence, that has also been detected by other techniques. The Einstein spacetime formalism uses a special definition of space and time coordinates that mandates light speed invariance for all observers, but which is easily misunderstood and misapplied.

Abstract
Cosmology, in its broadest sense, may be defined as the study of the universe in terms of its origin, its fundamental makeup, and its development in time. Many theories of cosmology have been proposed, and each assumes one or more models by which various phenomena, which are sensed by man or his instruments, are explained. Most of these theories and models are incomplete and thus leave room for alternate theories and explanations. Rhysmonic cosmology is a "new" theory which starts from fundamental premises and therefore builds-up a model of the universe from a firm foundation. It is the aim of this monograph to introduce the reader to these new concepts and to lead the reader in the development of this cosmology in a logical manner. The theory will not only explain much of what is assumed to be known of this universe, but will also develop new knowledge which will lead to testable predictions and perhaps new and fascinating technologies. The theory also provides logical explanations for many present day enigmas, especially those of an astronomical nature. While the author recognizes that this material is yet incomplete, sufficient information and data will be provided to enable many other independent investigations into this new cosmology. The author hopes that many opt to do so.

Ricardo Libertario Carezani (April 11, 1921 – 2016) was an Argentine-American physicist and the originator of Autodynamics (AD), an alternative theory of relativistic mechanics that he proposed as a replacement for Einstein's special and general relativity.
Biography
Carezani was born on April 11, 1921 in Córdoba, Argentina. He entered Tucumán University in 1939 to study electro-mechanical engineering, and from the outset regarded Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity as ill-founded. Around 1940 he came to believe that the "two observers in relative motion" postulate underlying special relativity was redundant; removing that redundancy, he argued, left a theory in which a single observer describes a phenomenon in its own coordinate system. By about 1945, at the age of 24, he considered the foundations of Autodynamics complete.
In 1951 Carezani published his first book on Autodynamics, which he said was immediately blacklisted by Argentina's National Atomic Energy Commission; only about 300 copies were printed. In August 1954 the Buenos Aires daily Crítica (which ceased publication in 1963) published an account of his theory; Carezani recounted that the paper's publisher was warned not to print anything further by him or face being shut down. He attributed the long delay in developing and publicising Autodynamics to this political climate — his struggle, as he put it, was waged against Perón on one side and the Einstein "myth" on the other.
After Argentina's political reopening, Carezani emigrated to the United States around 1979–1981, settling in California, where he worked as a mathematician and physicist. Richard Phillips Feynman (11 May 1918 – 15 February 1988) was an American theoretical physicist, one of the architects of renormalized quantum electrodynamics , and the source of the diagrammatic method that became the working language of particle physics. On this wiki he appears chiefly as the author of arguments that contributors here dispute, and as the physicist whose own doubts about renormalization are most often quoted back at the theory.
Feynman worked on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos, taught at Cornell from 1945 and at Caltech from 1950. Between 1947 and 1949 he, Julian Schwinger and Sin-Itiro Tomonaga independently produced formulations of quantum electrodynamics in which the divergent integrals of the theory are absorbed into redefinitions of the measured mass and charge of the electron; Freeman Dyson showed the three formulations to be equivalent, and the three shared the 1965 Nobel Prize. Feynman's route ran through his path-integral formulation of quantum mechanics, in which an amplitude is computed by summing a phase over every possible history, and through the diagrams that encode the terms of the perturbation expansion.
His other work includes the V−A theory of the weak interaction with Murray Gell-Mann (1958), the parton model of deep inelastic scattering (1969), an account of superfluid helium, and the 1959 lecture "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom", often cited as an origin point for nanotechnology. Robert E. Var is an American independent theoretical physicist based in Waltham, Massachusetts. Over nearly three decades he developed a programme — beginning with "space-energy theory" and culminating in "hyper-energy theory" — that treats space as a physical, energy-dense medium and seeks to derive gravity, relativity and cosmology from its dynamics.
Scientific work
Var's central idea is that space is not empty but a medium carrying an enormous intrinsic energy density, and that gravity is a local reduction of that density caused by mass — a principle he attributes to a gravitation theorem published by Maxwell in 1864. His first statement of the approach, " On a New Mathematical Framework for Fundamental Theoretical Physics ," appeared in the mainstream journal Foundations of Physics in 1975.
He later expanded it into a hierarchy of gauge-field theories: a velocity-dependent formulation he argues reproduces special relativity , a tensor "Einstein–Maxwell" theory he offers as a quantizable account of gravity, and finally hyper-energy theory , a many-dimensional cosmology in which the universe is a compressible medium of mass-energy with extra compactified dimensions sourced by the flow of time. He presents this framework as accounting for the big bang , cosmic inflation, the elementary-particle spectrum, and the physical nature of time and superstrings. This later work is largely unpublished and lies outside the scientific mainstream.

Golka (died 2018) was an American independent researcher and high-voltage experimenter, best known for Project Tesla — his decades-long effort to rebuild and extend Nikola Tesla 's Colorado Springs magnifying transmitter and to produce and study ball lightning in the laboratory. Working almost entirely outside universities and corporate laboratories, largely self-funded and using military surplus and salvaged parts, he built what was for years described as the world's largest Tesla coil, in an aircraft hangar at the former Wendover Air Force Base in Utah. He took seriously two propositions that mainstream physics had set aside — that ball lightning is a real, reproducible, self-contained plasma phenomenon with possible relevance to fusion, and that Tesla's scheme for wireless power transmission through the Earth-ionosphere cavity deserved to be tested rather than dismissed.
Biography
Golka was a native of Brockton, Massachusetts. His interest in Tesla was lifelong, and to obtain primary data he travelled to the Nikola Tesla Museum in Belgrade — reportedly on three separate occasions — to copy the inventor's Colorado Springs laboratory notes. Those notes became the working basis for his own reconstruction of Tesla's apparatus.
In the early 1970s he moved to Wendover, Utah, taking up residence in a large aircraft hangar at the deactivated Wendover Air Base, where he assembled his magnifying transmitter. He remained there for roughly nine years. In 1980 the U.S. Air Force transferred the inactive base to the town of Wendover; a very large increase in his rent followed, and after a period of disputes and litigation he left the site.

Abstract
Seismic waves are the most dramatic and most intensely studied manifestations of earthquakes. However, we also know of non-seismic phenomena, which precede large earthquakes. Some of them have been reported for centuries, even millennia. The list is long and diverse: bulging of the Earth's surface, changing well water levels, ground-hugging fog, low frequency electromagnetic emission, earthquake lights from ridges and mountain tops, magnetic field anomalies up to 0.5% of the Earth's dipole field, temperature anomalies by several degrees over wide areas as seen in satellite images, changes in the plasma density of the ionosphere, and strange animal behavior. Because it seems nearly impossible to imagine that such diverse phenomena could have a common physical cause, there is great confusion and even greater controversy. This explains why reports on nonseismic pre-earthquake phenomena are regarded with suspicion in the scientific community. This may change with the recent discovery that igneous and metamorphic rocks, which make up a major portion of the Earth's crust, contain electric charge carriers, which have been overlooked in the past. These charge carriers are defect electrons in the valence band, i.e., positive holes. Under normal conditions they are dormant, but when they "wake up", the rocks begin to sparkle and glow. This paper describes the physical and chemical nature of these positive holes, how they are introduced into minerals and rocks, and how they become activated. The Rodin coil is a toroidal winding pattern devised by Marko Rodin , in which the conductor is wound around a torus in a repeating star-like sequence rather than in the usual evenly spaced circular loops. It is one of the most widely replicated devices in the amateur new energy community, and a substantial body of experimental reports on it is catalogued on this wiki.
The winding
A conventional toroidal coil is wound so that successive turns lie side by side around the ring. In the Rodin pattern the winding instead skips a fixed number of positions on each pass, so that the conductor traces a closed star polygon over the surface of the torus and returns to its starting point only after several circuits. The result is that the current paths cross one another at intervals and the turns are not parallel, which is the feature its advocates regard as essential.
Rodin derived the sequence from what he calls vortex-based mathematics , a scheme built on the repeating digit-sum patterns that appear when the numbers 1–9 are doubled repeatedly (1, 2, 4, 8, 7, 5 and back to 1, with 3, 6 and 9 standing apart). He describes the winding as following "the longest free-flowing path of the electron", and identifies the 3–6–9 triad as governing a flux perpendicular to the coil surface.
Claims
Rodin and those following him have attributed a wide range of properties to the coil, including:
an unusually strong and well-collimated magnetic field along the torus axis, described as a toroidal pinch ;
applications to fusion confinement, brushless motors, high-sensitivity antennas and propulsion;
in the stronger versions of the claim, gravitational effects and energy gain.

Roger J. Anderton is an English independent researcher, writer and translator based in the United Kingdom, known for his work on theoretical physics, unified field theory and the philosophy of the natural sciences. His writing pays particular attention to the physics of Newton, Boscovich and Einstein. In addition to writing his own articles, he translates, edits and publishes books, and he is best known as a modern champion of the 18th-century unified field theory of the Jesuit polymath Roger Joseph Boscovich (Ruđer Bošković, 1711–1787).

He is remembered above all for his Philosophiae naturalis theoria redacta ad unicam legem virium in natura existentium ("Theory of Natural Philosophy reduced to the single law of forces existing in nature", Vienna 1758), in which he reduced the whole of physics to one universal force law acting between non-extended point particles — the first fully worked-out unified theory of matter and force.

Boscovich's theory has also been championed by the Serbian polymer scientist Dragoslav Stoiljković, Anderton's principal collaborator.

In March 1989, Roger Stringham of First Gate Energies, in Hawaii, USA pioneered the method of using acoustic cavitation to produce the cold fusion effect. Acoustic cavitation uses ultrasonic waves to create gas bubbles within the heavy water. Stringham was the first to use the term "sonofusion" to describe how this phenomenon creates energy in cold fusion experiments.
This work is not be confused with other experiments in the hot fusion field which also use a form of acoustic cavitation, called "acoustic inertial confinement fusion." The two types of research are markedly different.
The key differences with the cold fusion method, sonofusion, is that the effect is directly related to an as-yet-unknown interaction between heavy water and a host metal, such as palladium. The hot fusion method does not employ a host metal. The other key distinction between the cold fusion and hot fusion method is that the cold fusion method produces no deadly neutron radiation, as occurs in hot fusion. -- Steven B. Roland H. Dishington (1919 – 15 January 2016) was an American physicist who spent much of his career in the aerospace industry at TRW , and who developed over several decades an independent programme in which matter, charge and energy are all distributions and distortions of a single aether .
His work is unusually coherent for an independent programme: a small number of commitments, applied consistently across electromagnetism, particle structure and the conservation laws, and set out across four books and a series of papers. He argued the case in the technical language of classical field theory rather than by analogy, and his most-read paper is addressed directly to what he considered errors in the standard textbooks .
The aether as the one substance
Dishington's starting point is that space and matter are not two things. In The Extended Electron he describes matter and space as disproportionate distributions of the aether — the same substance, differently concentrated — and in Energy and Charge he accounts for energy and charge as distortions of that substance.
His stated method is worth recording, because it explains the shape of everything he wrote:
If there is no picture to illustrate a theory, constructing one and backing it up with a strong, simple-as-possible mathematical representation is the way to get to new technologies in the shortest time.
— Roland H. Dishington, The Extended Electron
That is the demand for intelligibility that runs through most of the work catalogued on this wiki — a theory should admit of a picture, and the mathematics should represent the picture rather than replace it. See Aether .

Ron Forth is a Canadian mechanical and petroleum engineer, author, and amateur astronomer based in the Calgary area of Alberta, Canada. After a career of some forty years in the energy industry, he turned to theoretical physics and cosmology, publishing an alternative cosmological model that he presents as a resolution to several outstanding problems in modern physics.
Biography
Forth holds a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering and spent about forty years working across several areas of the energy sector, describing himself professionally as a petroleum engineer. He lives in the Calgary area of Alberta, and is an amateur astronomer with a longstanding interest in the Electric Universe concept, cosmology, the Ether, energy, and quantum mechanics. Now retired, he has said that much of his cosmological thinking developed during evening walks under starlit skies. In 2023 he published the book The Forth Dimension: A Hitchhiker's Guide to the Universe through FriesenPress.

Following the 2010 Deepwater Horizon (BP) oil spill, Carat became an advocate for clean energy from cold fusion. That year she founded Cold Fusion Now! , which she has largely self-funded, to build a public presence for scientists working in the field.

Through Cold Fusion Now! , Carat has written more than 300 articles and produced podcasts, video interviews and documentary material on the history of cold fusion and LENR research. Biography
Published sources say little about Gries's personal background, and this article does not speculate about it. What is documented is his research practice. RWGresearch was created, in his own description, "to help Russ promote his work, share his results and work as a team with his subscribers", and it operates as a small home laboratory funded by viewer donations and built largely from salvaged parts. He has emphasised that serious experimental work does not require an institutional budget, noting for example that "old CRT TVs and computer monitors people are throwing out every day have a lot of good magnet wire in them", and that most of his early coils were wound from recycled material at essentially no cost.
He maintains the RWGresearch website and forum presence, broadcasts live experimental sessions, and for several years ran an annual community "Pulse Motor Build-Off" (documented from 2012 to 2020) in which participants built and compared competing motor designs.

"SN 1987A and the Neutrino" is a paper by Ricardo L Carezani challenging the neutrino detections associated with the supernova of February 1987 in the Large Magellanic Cloud — the observation generally regarded as the founding event of neutrino astronomy. Carezani sets out seven numbered "facts" against it.
Overview
Carezani begins from a published summary of the evidence: "The coincidence between the two results provides OVERWHELMING evidence that the neutrinos, formed at the instant the supernova's core collapsed, did INDEED come from this star". His objection is first to the form of the argument — "We suppose what we are trying to prove: neutrinos!" — and then to the data behind it.
The argument
The seven facts
Fact 1. Of four detectors then operating, one — Mont Blanc — recorded the first claimed burst, at 02:52:36.8 UT. IMB, Kamiokande II and the South Dakota experiment did not. Twenty-five per cent agreement, Carezani argues, is not overwhelming evidence.
Fact 2. Even granting simultaneity between Mont Blanc and Kamiokande II, two of four detectors saw nothing, so the agreement is at best 50 per cent.
Fact 3. Producing the assumed flux from 180,000 light years away requires converting 10 to 15 per cent of a solar mass to neutrinos. No mechanism for this is supplied, and the mechanism would differ from anything known in stars.
Fact 4. To explain neutrinos arriving at Kamiokande II twelve seconds after the first burst, a "neutrino sphere" some tens of kilometres in radius is invoked to trap and release them. Published 1992
Volume 3

Abstract
The Einstein theory is sometimes incorrectly accused of being unable to explain the Sagnac effect (even for an unclosed path configuration). However, its explanation reveals that it works with the gravitational field as the equivalent of an ether, in which the velocity of light is not constant unless space is distorted into a non-Euclidean geometry so as to force its constancy. Although not wrong in the sense of disagreeing with experimental results, this mathematical formalism is complicated, opaque and unnecessary, for it is easily replaced by very simple mathematics in Euclidean space yielding the same result when it is assumed that the velocity of light is constant with respect to the local gravitational field; this requires no special non-Euclidean space.

filename: Satellite Motion in a Non-Singular Gravitational Potential.html

Title Satellite Motion in a Non-Singular Gravitational Potential
Author(s) Ioannis Iraklis Haranas , Spiros Pagiatakis
Keywords Non-singular potential, Lagrange
search_text:
Title Satellite Motion in a Non-Singular Gravitational Potential
Author(s) Ioannis Iraklis Haranas , Spiros Pagiatakis
Keywords Non-singular potential, Lagrange planetary, equations, Disturbing potential, Eccentricity functions, Hansen coefficients ? GRACE?
Published 2010
Journal Vixra
Volume Astrophys Space Sci, Volume 3
No. of pages 7
Abstract
We study the effects of a non-singular gravitational potential on satellite orbits by deriving the corresponding time rates of change of its orbital elements. This is achieved by expanding the non-singular potential into power series up to second order. This series contains three terms, the first been the Newtonian potential and the other two, here R1 (first order term) and R2 (second order term), express deviations of the singular potential from the Newtonian. These deviations from the Newtonian potential are taken as disturbing potential terms in the Lagrange planetary equations that provide the time rates of change of the orbital elements of a satellite in a non-singular gravitational field. We split these effects into secular, low and high frequency components and we evaluate them numerically using the low Earth orbiting mission Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE). We show that the secular effect of the secondorder disturbing term R2 on the perigee and the mean anomaly are 4 .307 ? 10−9/a, and −2 .533 ? 10−15/a, respectively. These effects are far too small and most likely cannot easily be observed with today's technology. Numerical evaluation of the low and high frequency effects of the disturbing term R2 on low Earth orbiters like GRACE are very small and undetectable by current observational means

Summary
Nobody came into the live room, so Franklin Hu ran what he called a mailbag: reading out the week's email correspondence on the nature of light and answering it, with comments coming in from the stream. Carl was on air; Roger Anderton was watching. It is a one-sided session, but it collects the arguments Hu returns to more compactly than any other.
Rydin's questions

We have invented wave mechanics to help us visualise a process, he wrote, and that does not make it so.

An open chat hosted by Franklin Hu with Ian Cohen, James Keene , Stoyan Sarg , Cornelis Verhey , Bob and Jim, with comments from Harry Ricker , Curt Renshaw and Alistair Riddoch on the stream. The topic had been running all week on the email list: the standard textbook picture of an electromagnetic wave — electric and magnetic vectors at right angles, in phase, propagating through empty space — and whether anything of the sort actually happens. Hu put the diagram on screen and asked the room.
The objections to the picture
Bob had two. The first is energy: square the two fields and add them, and the total goes to zero at the nodes and back to a maximum, which he cannot reconcile with conservation. The second came from his reading of Jefimenko , who argues that Maxwell's equations are not causal. Once retardation is put in properly, a changing electric field does not cause a changing magnetic field, nor the reverse; the charges are the source of both, and the two merely propagate together, which is why they look like cause and effect. He added that the picture omits the longitudinal Coulomb component that an oscillating source charge must produce.
Hu pressed the same point geometrically. If there is a source, the field should fall off as the inverse square, which the picture does not show; and the only way to get vectors pointing uniformly perpendicular, rather than radially from a point, would be a flat charged plate cycling between plus and minus five volts, with a rectangular magnet reversing alongside it. He said he found that hard to believe.

An open chat hosted by Franklin Hu with Harry Ricker , Ian Cohen, James Keene , Carl, Bob and others, a fortnight into the lockdowns. The first hour went on the pandemic, the second on inertia; the two halves turned out to be about the same thing.
Is it legitimate to question a medical consensus?
Ian put the question that framed the session. Dissidents make a practice of questioning consensus in physics; medicine now presents an international consensus of the same kind, with politicians deferring wholly to it. Is scepticism appropriate here, or irresponsible? His own answer was that the human pressures are identical — careers ended for stepping out of line, funding tied to producing the expected numbers — and that if anything they operate more strongly in a less exact science. He drew a list of what he called secular apocalypses he had lived through: acid rain, the ozone hole, the exhaustion of fossil fuels, Y2K, global warming and then climate change, SARS and Ebola, weapons of mass destruction — each in its turn the end of the world, each questionable only at the sceptic's cost.
Ricker's version was drier: we are at the bottom of the food chain, told to believe the media, which produces experts, who are presumed to know. Whether certified experts can be wrong is the legitimate question, and we cannot tell from here.
Hu's own scepticism was narrower and concrete. He could not reconcile the advice not to wear masks with the effort to secure masks for health workers, nor with other countries handing them out; and the shortages had not eased in weeks. Summary
An open chat hosted by Franklin Hu with Ian Cohen, James Keene and Cornelis Verhey , with Bill Lucas commenting from the YouTube stream. It started from a small puzzle Ian had been chewing on and ran, by a chain of ordinary steps, to the structure of the vacuum and the Michelson–Gale experiment.
Viscosity, and what it says about mass
Ian's puzzle: liquids grow less viscous as they warm — treacle in January against treacle in June, the oil in an engine — but gases do the opposite, and he had checked it twice, latterly against Jeans's Dynamical Theory of Gases , because it sounded wrong. Nobody in the room could account for the inversion; Hu had expected heat to loosen the bonds in both cases.
Hu's way of thinking about it was mechanical: a rack dragged across a table crowded with billiard balls, the resistance set by how many balls are in the way; add glue to the balls and the sticking matters more when they move slowly, which gives the liquid behaviour. The discussion passed through what distinguishes a solid from a liquid — Hu's criterion being that the bonds hold their geometry regardless of external energy, which is why one solid will not pass through another — and Ian's correction that the state is not a property of the substance, since water takes all three.
That produced the session's key move. If a spoon meets more resistance in molasses than in water, and mass is defined by force over acceleration, then the mass of a marble is not a property of the marble but of the marble against its medium. Hu pressed this deliberately: what he calls matter is the marble; mass is only what we measure when it moves through something.
